name: ECG-Expert-QA
description: Reliable and interpretable electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis has long been a grand challenge in medical artificial intelligence, requiring complex reasoning, ethical awareness, and multimodal understanding. Despite recent progress in large language models (LLMs), three major limitations persist. First, existing ECG datasets primarily focus on static classification or single-turn QA, lacking support for interactive and context-dependent reasoning. Second, current evaluation frameworks overlook ethical and patient-centered perspectives, failing to capture responsibility and safety in diagnostic reasoning. Third, real-world diagnostic diversity and data imbalance remain underrepresented, limiting model robustness and generalization. To address these issues, we present ECG-Expert-QA, a unified multimodal benchmark for diagnostic reasoning and conversational evaluation of medical LLMs. It integrates real-world ECG records with systematically synthesized cases, covering 12 diagnostic tasks and 47,211 expert-validated QA pairs. The benchmark uniquely supports multi-turn doctor-patient dialogues, ethical risk assessment, and cross-modal clinical reasoning, enabling comprehensive evaluation across reasoning depth and contextual understanding. We further conduct extensive benchmarking of mainstream medical LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen2.5) and fine-tuning experiments on the lightweight MiniMind2, demonstrating that ECG-Expert-QA effectively differentiates model capabilities in semantic comprehension, clinical reasoning, and ethical expression. Built upon a knowledge-guided and roledriven generation framework, ECG-Expert-QA ensures linguistic precision and clinical fidelity. The dataset has been fully opensourced on GitHub (available at: https://github.com/Zaozzz/ECG-Expert-QA), providing a reproducible foundation for developing trustworthy, explainable, and patient-centered medical LLMs.
reputation: New and growing—open-sourced and gaining attention in the medical LLM community for ECG-specific diagnostic and conversational evaluation.
notes: Includes real patient ECGs and synthesized cases—potential privacy/contamination risk; intended for research use only and not a substitute for clinical validation; evaluation mixes automated and human-reviewed metrics.
